brief: A color palette generator that works like a musical instrument — play colors, harmonies lock like chords

dominant_strengths: Confident dark canvas with gradient swatches creates immediate visceral appeal and lets color samples breathe legibly
Clear three-zone layout: harmonies grid, harmony-type controls, export list — easy scanning and fast comprehension
Hex labels embedded on swatches with subtle pill backgrounds show competent micro-craft and informational hierarchy
dominant_weaknesses: Hex codes are clipped/truncated on every swatch (#F56B6B becomes #F56R6R-like), a critical legibility failure undermining utility
The 'musical instrument / chords' metaphor is entirely absent — no staff, keys, audio cues, or chord-play affordance visible
Generic SaaS chrome (purple gradient logo, standard buttons, export rows with arrows) makes it feel like any palette tool, not distinctive
fix_priorities: Fix swatch label rendering and contrast so hex values are fully readable — core function is currently broken
Express the musical metaphor visually: keyboard/fretboard input, chord-shaped harmony selectors, audible feedback on hover
Differentiate harmony-type buttons beyond a generic 2x3 grid — map them to chord diagrams or interval shapes
Tighten typography scale; the 'Color Harmonies' title competes with sidebar headers without a clear hierarchy
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral hit from gradient swatches, mediocre behavioral layer due to broken labels, and shallow reflective payoff because the promised musical concept never materializes.
rationale.intent_fit: Functions as a competent palette generator but completely fails the brief's distinctive promise of color-as-instrument — the chord/play metaphor is invisible.
